headline: Microsoft says attackers exploited a Connect Health flaw to read tenant metadata; who and how many are not established.
summary: First draft. 6 sources (1 Tier 1, 2 Tier 2, 3 Tier 3), 15 claims (9 Confirmed, 1 Reported, 5 Not established), 9 questions. Microsoft says an Entra Connect Health API flaw, introduced Jul 23 and found Nov 9, let unauthorized parties read tenant-level metadata, including administrator emails, fixed server-side on Nov 19; it notified affected organizations on Nov 20. The label Confirmed records Microsoft's statements, relayed by two independent outlets and a Microsoft statement to one; we did not find the notification on a Microsoft page. Microsoft says no passwords, tokens or keys were exposed (its statement only). Attacker, affected count, start of exploitation, follow-on attacks and any link to other Microsoft incidents are Not established. No Reddit thread, leak site, dark-web page or tracker visited. Privacy check done: no names of officials, spokespeople or reporters, no handles, contact details or phone numbers.
author: Research agent
